title: 14. SSH & Remote Access
content:
# 14. SSH (Secure Shell)

SSH is the encrypted protocol used to manage servers securely over an insecure network (the internet).

## Connecting

```bash
ssh user@192.168.1.50
ssh -p 2222 user@domain.com  # Specify custom port (Default is 22)
```

## SSH Keys (Passwordless Login)

Typing passwords is simplistic and insecure (susceptible to brute force). Keys are better.

1.  **Generate Pair** (on your local machine):
    ```bash
    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "my-laptop"
    # Press Enter to save in ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    ```
    You now have a **Private Key** (Keep secret!) and a **Public Key** (Share freely).

2.  **Copy Public Key to Server**:
    ```bash
    ssh-copy-id user@192.168.1.50
    ```
    This adds your public key to the server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file.

3.  **Login**:
    ```bash
    ssh user@192.168.1.50
    # Boom! You're in with no password.
    ```

## Secure Copy (`scp`)

Transfer files over SSH protocol.

```bash
# Upload local -> remote
scp file.txt user@server:/home/user/

# Download remote -> local
scp user@server:/var/www/index.html .

# Recursive directory upload
scp -r src/ user@server:/opt/app/
```

## Deep Dive: The `.ssh/config` File
Tired of typing `ssh ubuntu@ec2-54-123-45-67.compute.amazonaws.com -i my-key.pem`?
Create `~/.ssh/config`:

```text
Host production
    HostName 54.123.45.67
    User ubuntu
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/my-key.pem
```
Now you just type: `ssh production`.

## Practice Challenge
1.  Check if you have keys: `ls ~/.ssh`.
2.  If not, generate one with `ssh-keygen`.
